verification.scope: Attempt, lease, cursor, fencing, idempotency, and cancellation domain
verification.result: Browser/API fault acceptance and the Domain API integration suite proved failure, retry, monotonic fencing, stale callback rejection, ordered cursor progression, and observable cancellation convergence.
Go tests passed stable RunWorkflow identity, signal deduplication, phase transitions, replay-safe carried state, outbox routing, and Continue-As-New behavior.
DB migration, shared validators, Go API, TypeScript client/read model, and Runs UI were compiled and exercised together on the migrated local database.

Typecheck, build, migration checks, token gates, Go tests, and formatting checks passed. Full Vitest passed 4737 tests; its only three failures were inherited concurrent port-ownership timing cases, and all 28 tests in that file passed serially.

residual_risks: Independent engineering review and product-owner acceptance are required before approval, release, or ship claims.
G1 migration 0234 remains a production rolling-upgrade blocker for the combined branch until expand/contract or a stopped-write maintenance window is approved.

G2.2 authenticates the local executor through the board-authenticated HostTrusted server facade and an executor identity header; remote runner credentials, transport trust, and fleet enrollment remain G3 scope.
Temporal behavior is covered by unit and dispatcher tests, but this acceptance did not launch an external Temporal server and kill/restart a live worker process.
The product-native Artifact, Evidence, DeliveryReview, and Acceptance write surfaces are not implemented, so a succeeded or canceled Run cannot close the runtime Target beyond draft/Define.
